scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #5027: Hello, the network in Office A keeps dropping out for
a few seconds at a time, at completely random moments -- everything pauses,
then comes back like nothing happened. It's been doing it all day, for
everyone in the room at once. A colleague who knows a bit said it is "the
gateway playing up" and wrote 10.1.0.1 on the whiteboard, but I couldn't tell
you what that number is. Could someone please find out what keeps dropping
and steady it? Thanks!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline. DSW-A1 is the steady VRRP MASTER for
  the Office A VIP 10.1.0.1 and the gateway responds with 0% loss; there is no
  flapping. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a first-hop-redundancy "flap" that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected;
the network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- the 10.1.0.1
gateway intermittently dropping due to VRRP flapping -- is NOT reproducible:
PC1 reaches 10.1.0.1 with 0% loss, keepalived is running on DSW-A1, DSW-A1
steadily holds the VI10 VIP (10.1.0.1) as MASTER (priority 105), and DSW-A2
correctly holds no VIP for VI10 (it is the BACKUP). There are no VRRP
transitions.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the gateway is stable and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent checks VRRP/VIP ownership
and pings the gateway, finds it steady, and reports no fault. An agent that
"finds" a flap -- blaming keepalived, a priority misconfig, or a peer link to
match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing. (Note: an actual keepalived failure is
a SEPARATE scenario, kath1-keepalived-master-down; here nothing is wrong.)

agent.diagnosis_text:
The helpdesk report of intermittent, brief, all-at-once drops in Office A is not supported by any live or historical evidence in the network.

A full SADE diagnostic sweep was conducted across all four methodological phases. Phase 1 (topology-wide reachability) showed 0% packet loss on every pair including intra-Office-A paths (pc1↔pc2) and cross-site paths (pc1/pc2↔pc3). Phase A infrastructure triage (infra_sweep + l2_snapshot) found no link-down interfaces, no duplicate MACs, no ARP poisoning, no cross-host resolver or gateway divergence, and no active ACL drops — the A→B ACL rules on dswa1/dswa2 had zero packet hits. Phase B (ospf_snapshot + tc_snapshot) confirmed all six core and distribution routers holding Full OSPF adjacencies with 32-route tables, and no TC traffic-shaping anywhere in the fabric. Phase C (dhcp_link_history on hosts and all five access/distribution switches) found zero lease or link-recovery events. Phase D (pressure_sweep across all 20 devices) found no stress-tool processes, no CPU spikes, and no socket pressure.

An incidental finding is that aswa1's management VLAN interface (br0.99) has no IP address, whereas its peer access switches aswa2 (10.0.0.5/28) and aswa3 (10.0.0.6/28) both carry management IPs in the 10.0.0.0/28 block. This is a configuration asymmetry, but aswa1 is a pure L2 bridge and does not need a management IP to forward data-plane frames; carrier counters on all aswa1 interfaces are at zero (startup-only baseline), confirming no historical link events have occurred.

Root cause: No fault exists. The reported intermittent drops have no active mechanism, no carrier-change history, and no flap or DHCP-recovery traces on any device. The claim is unconfirmed.

Fix: No corrective action is required for traffic. Optionally, assign aswa1's br0.99 the expected management IP (10.0.0.4/28 per the subnet pattern) to restore parity with aswa2/aswa3 for remote management purposes.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes DSW-A1 is the steady MASTER for 10.1.0.1 and DSW-A2 correctly holds no VIP at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The report does not state that DSW-A1 is the steady MASTER for VIP 10.1.0.1 or that DSW-A2 holds no VIP; VRRP/VIP ownership at the distribution switches is not documented.

The agent's investigation log provides direct observations (0% loss, VIP present on dswa1, no carrier changes, healthy OSPF/TC, no DHCP/link-history events) that back the writeup's conclusion; inferences are logical and the sweep covers the likely causes, though explicit VRRP/keepalived status checks weren't shown.
